A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same counterfactual reasoning study. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression experiments, architecture and data-diversity analyses, and Lotka–Volterra simulations in Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v2 reports revised synthetic experiments and additional latent-variable probes, training-emergence results, attention-head analyses, and an observational-continuation comparison.

M1.justification: The core counterfactual prompting framework, autoregressive prediction procedure, and MSE objective remain. The designated noise-abduction head is identified in a trained Transformer, not installed as a new architectural component. Optimizer, model-size, and data-generation revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Appendix E.5 adds observational-continuation regression as a control task with a different prediction requirement. Linear, tanh, sigmoid, multiplicative-noise, and Lotka–Volterra counterfactual tasks remain. The new clinical illustration does not constitute evaluation on clinical data.

E2.justification: v2 adds an ordinary-least-squares counterfactual reference in Section 4.4 and an observational-continuation-trained GPT-2 comparator in Appendix E.5. The existing GPT-2, LSTM, GRU, and Elman RNN comparison families remain; their configuration changes belong to E3.

E3.justification: Reported regression training changes from 200,000 to 50,000 steps and Adam to AdamW; recurrent models change from three to two layers, and evaluation samples increase from 100 to 6,400. Context-length settings also change. Appendix F revises SDE parameterization, sampling times, training budget, and batch size, while the new probing and emergence experiments introduce additional protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds residual-stream probes for theta and beta, training-phase analyses across embedding dimensions, variable-index noise-abduction head inspection, and an observational-continuation control. The SDE attention analysis is revised. Conversely, v1's E=20–250 convergence discussion and its 15/20/25-time-point SDE performance comparison are not retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use basic-bootstrap uncertainty reporting, including 95% intervals for data-diversity plots. Moving uncertainty bands from v1's appendix into v2's main figures does not introduce a new statistical practice. Neither version reports independent training-run or seed counts; larger evaluation samples are an E3 change.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised and expanded. Table 1's Full Transformer multiplicative-noise MSE changes from 0.0437 to 0.0364, and GPT-2 changes from the highest Lotka–Volterra MSE in v1 Figure 5a to the lowest in v2 Figure 6a. Experimental conditions also change, so these are not same-setting performance gains. New probing, emergence, head-localization, and continuation-comparison findings are reported.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 1 on counterfactual identifiability, its assumptions and proof, and supporting bijective-mechanism results in Appendix B. Appendices F.2–F.3 add parameter-bound and initialization derivations. Lemma 1's domains and argument ordering are corrected. However, the revised main-text Lotka–Volterra f/g assignments conflict with Appendix F's x/y equations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add central claims about counterfactual identifiability, linear representation of latent concepts, and an emergent index-dependent noise-abduction head. These substantially extend v1's emphasis on demonstrated counterfactual prediction and the importance of attention, depth, and data diversity.

C2.justification: v2 develops a substantially fuller mechanism account, linking latent decoding to the Linear Representation Hypothesis and lower counterfactual error to recoverable noise. It interprets extended-training transitions and designated heads as evidence of noise abduction. Appendix F.4 also newly acknowledges that reusing only 20 time grids compromises the stated exchangeability setup.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands SDE parameterization, initial-condition, and batch-generation instructions, including disclosure of time-grid reuse. It supplies probe training/evaluation sizes and long-training head-inspection details, and revises optimizer and runtime information. The code pointer changes from moXmiller/counterfactual-reasoning to mrtzmllr/iccr; the PDFs alone do not establish either repository's availability.

R1.justification: v2 positions its identifiability theorem as an extension of Nasr-Esfahany et al. and connects its mechanistic findings to Park et al.'s Linear Representation Hypothesis. Added discussions cover emergence, recurrent-model copying, compositional depth, and data diversity. These changes substantially broaden the research positioning beyond isolated citation additions.

P1.justification: The seven-section outline and Appendices A–G remain. Local rewrites update the abstract and contributions, replace semantic-ambiguity examples with patient-treatment motivation, repurpose Section 4.4, and reorganize Appendix F. Acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist are added, while much of the existing exposition is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned around a clinical example, and the separate ambiguity-resolution illustration is removed. v2 adds probe plots, emergence curves, regression-head heatmaps, and a continuation comparison. Existing uncertainty displays are consolidated into main-text figures, while SDE plots and attention maps are redrawn. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new held-out probes, index-dependent attention maps, and continuation control provide more direct support for the noise-abduction interpretation than v1's architecture comparisons. Expanded implementation disclosures improve transparency. These gains are qualified by removed large-dimension and context-length checks and new SDE reporting inconsistencies: Section 5 swaps f/g relative to Appendix F, and Figure 6a's caption says 0.1 where its bars are approximately 0.01. The net improvement is therefore limited.
